 JUDGMENT 1.

Briefly stated that the case of the prosecution against the accused is that on 17.09.2013, at about 5.30 pm, at Sultanpur Karala Road, near Peer Baba ki Mazar, Kabristan, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of Police Station Kanjhawala, accused was driving the vehicle/tempo bearing no.
DL1LP-0445 in a rash and negligent manner and while driving the same, he hit against one car bearing no. DL5CJ-2586 and caused grievous injuries to Ramu and death (not amounting to culpable homicide) of Kishan and also he was using a fake license at that time on this basis, the present FIR was registered against the accused.
Upon completion of investigation, charge sheet u/s 279/338/304A/420/468/471 IPC was filed against the accused and he was sent for trial.
2. The Ld. Predecessor of this court took cognizance of the offence and issued process against the accused.
Pursuant to the appearance of the accused, he was supplied with the copy of chargesheet in compliance of Section 207 CrPC.
Upon hearing the arguments, vide order dated 20.07.2023 charge under Section 279/338/304A/471 IPC was ordered to be framed against accused.

1 pleaded not guilty and the matter was listed for Prosecution Evidence ('PE').
3. In order to establish its case against the accused, prosecution has examined three witnesses in toto.

4. PW1 Sh. Sourav Bhattacharyya official from Department of Public Vehicle brought an authority letter Ex PW1/A and gave report with regard to driving license bearing no. WB-0120020586592 vide Ex. PW1/B and submitted that according to the report, no such DL has ever been issued.
The witness was not cross examined by Ld. Defence counsel despite opportunity granted.

5. PW2 Retd. ASI Raghunath deposed that on 17.09.2013, he received DD No. 78B and he alongwitih HC Ramkesh reached at the spot i.e., Karla Sultanpur Road, Near Peer Baba Majar where one tempo bearing no. DL1LP-0445 and one maurti Van bearing no. DL5CJ-2586 were found in accidental condition and injured has taken to hospital.
He further deposed that after leaving Ct.
Ramkesh

at the spot, he went to SGM Hospital where he collected the MLC no. 17014/13 of Kishan and 17013/13 of Ramu but they were not in a condition to give their statement and thereafter, he came back to the spot.

He further deposed that he prepared the rukka Ex. PW2/A, both abovesaid vehicle were seized vide memo Ex. PW2/B and PW2/C, prepared the site plan Ex. PW2/D and deposited the case property in the malkhana and in the PS, he received DD No. 30A regarding the death of injured Kishan and thereafter the investigation was handed over to SI Sudhir Rathi.
The witness was not cross examined by Ld.
Defence counsel
despite opportunity granted.

6. PW3 Retd. ASI Jai Karan deposed that on 20.09.2013, he served notice u/s. 133 M. V. Act Ex.
PW3/A to the owner of the offending vehicle Sita Ram who produced the accused in the PS on 01.10.2013.
He further deposed that accused was correctly identified by the injured PW Ramu who also came to PS to inquire about his case.

He further deposed that he arrested the accused vide memo Ex. PW3/A and verified the necessary documents from concerned authorities, mechanically inspected both the vehicles, obtain the final opinion on the MLC of injured Raju which was found to be grievous.

He further deposed that he added section 468/471 IPC in the present case as the DL of the accused was never issued to him by Transport Department Kolkata and accused was again arrested vide memo Ex. PW3/C and was produced before the court and sent to JC.
He further submitted that he collected the PM report, filed DAR, prepared the present charge sheet and filed the same before the court.
The witness was not cross examined by Ld. Defence counsel despite opportunity granted.

7. Vide separate statement u/s 294 CrPC, accused has admitted supardarinama of offending vehicle,
MLC NO. 17013/13 & 17014/13 both dt. 17.9.2013, PM report 930/13, dt. 18.9.2013, X-ray report of MLC No. 17013/13, original FIR, DD No. 78B Dt. 17.9.13 & register no. 19 vide Ex. A1 to A8 respectively.

2 8. Accordingly, vide order dated 16.02.2024, PE was closed.
In the statement recorded u/s. 313 CrPC, accused denied the case of the prosecution and pleaded innocence.
He stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He did not opt to lead defence evidence.
9. Ms. Tanya Uppal, Ld. APP has prayed that the accused be convicted.
10. Per Contra, Sh. Ratnakar Maltiyar Ld.
Counsel for the accused has submitted that accused is completely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
At the end, he has submitted that the prosecution has completely failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and therefore, the accused is liable to be acquitted of the alleged offence.
11.Before discussing the testimonies of PWs, it would be prudent to discuss the legal position involved in the present case.
Legal Framework 12.Section 279 IPC provides for the offence of rash driving or riding on a public way.

It reads as under:
"Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both."
13.Section 337/338/304A IPC provide for the offences of causing hurt/grievous hurt/death by an act endangering life or personal safety of others.
These provisions are the consequences of a rash or negligent act of driving on a public way punishable u/s 279 IPC.
"337. Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others -

Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
**

*
338. Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others -

Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both."

3 *** 304A

Causing death by negligence - Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

14.For an offence u/s 279/338/304A IPC, prosecution is required to prove the following ingredients:
a. Identity of the accused being the driver of the offending vehicle.
b. That the alleged accident is the result of rash and negligent driving of the accused at a public place.
c. The rash and negligent driving of the accused resulted in injury/death of deceased.
15.Now
, coming to the facts of the present case.
Unfortunately, the only eye witness in the present case had expired during the trial.
He could not be examined.
Therefore, as far as the offence under section 279/338/304A IPC is concerned, there is no material on record against the accused.
The testimony of remaining PWs is not sufficient to fasten guilt on the accused.
PW2 had reached the spot well after the incident and he did not find any eye witness at the spot.
PW3 had taken up the investigation subsequently and carried out further investigation at the instance of the injured who expired subsequently.
Therefore, the identity of the accused as the driver of the offending vehicle remains doubtful.
16. Now, turning to the application of Section 471 of the IPC.
This provision pertains to the use of any document as genuine, despite knowing or believing it to be forged.
To establish the offense under Section 471, the prosecution presented two witnesses.
PW3 testified that the accused was brought to the police station by the owner of the offending vehicle, after which the accused's driving license was seized.
PW1 further testified that the driving license allegedly seized from the accused had never been issued by the competent authority.
17.Upon analyzing the record, it becomes clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the accused's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt under this section.
The essential requirement for culpability under Section 471 IPC is the use of a forged document as genuine (Parshadi Lal v. NCT of Delhi 2012 SCC OnLine Del 6426).

entities.text: Parshadi Lal v. NCT of Delhi 2012 SCC OnLine Del 6426
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case, there is no evidence of any "use" of the document by the accused,
which constitutes the actus reus of the offense.
The prosecution merely asserts that the driving license was seized from the accused but does not provide any evidence that the document was used for any purpose by the accused.
The identity of the accused as the driver of the offending vehicle has already been observed to be doubtful.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to indicate that the accused had used the said document.
18.Furthermore, the prosecution has failed to establish the necessary mens rea, or guilty intent, on the part of the accused.
There is no evidence to show that the accused knew or had reason to believe that the document was forged.
Without proving both the actus reus and the mens rea, it cannot be concluded that the accused is culpable under Section 471 IPC.
As a result, no offence under this section can be established.

4 19.In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.

20.Thus, in view of the foregoing analysis, the accused Shambhu Tanti S/o Karu Tanti is held not guilty and stands acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 279/338/304A/471 IPC.
